title: Ferroelectric-controllable spin-orbit torque in two-dimensional multiferroic heterostructure
authors: Weiyi Pan, Gusthavo M. S. Brizolla, Jaroslav Fabian
abstract: Spin-orbit torque (SOT), which enables electrical control of magnetization, plays a crucial role in the development of next-generation spintronic devices. Realizing SOT in two-dimensional van der Waals systems, together with achieving efficient nonvolatile manipulation via ferroelectricity, would be highly beneficial for the implementation of tunable logic devices with enhanced storage density. In this work, based on first-principles calculation and using a multiferroic Fe$_{3}$GeTe$_{2}$/In$_{2}$Se$_{3}$ heterostructure as a representative example, we demonstrate that switching the ferroelectric polarization of the In$_{2}$Se$_{3}$ layer induces a pronounced modification in the magnetization-dependent distribution of torkance within the heterostructure. Specifically, when the magnetization is in the plane, where the torque is maximal, reversing the polarization of In$_{2}$Se$_{3}$ from upward to downward enhances the total torkance to more than 150% of its original value. This substantial variation primarily originates from the polarization-induced modulation of the $z$ component of the time-reversal-odd torkance, which is mainly associated with an approximately 233% change in the atomic-resolved torque contributed from the middle Fe layer in Fe$_{3}$GeTe$_{2}$ layer. Further analysis reveals that the electronic states near $Γ$ on the Fermi surface undergo significant reconstruction upon polarization switching, which is responsible for the observed variation in the time-reversal-odd torque. Our results not only provide new insights into the functional potential of van der Waals multiferroic heterostructures, but also offer a viable strategy for achieving electrically tunable SOT, paving the way for future programmable spintronic devices.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates that ferroelectric polarization switching in a 2D multiferroic heterostructure ($	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2/	ext{In}_2	ext{Se}_3$) can dramatically enhance the Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT). By calculating the torkance using first-principles methods, the authors show that this polarization control offers a viable pathway toward developing programmable and energy-efficient spintronic memory devices.
main_problem: The goal is to achieve electrically tunable Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT) for next-generation spintronic devices by leveraging the coupling between ferroelectricity and magnetism in 2D multiferroic heterostructures.
main_result: Reversing the ferroelectric polarization in an $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2/	ext{In}_2	ext{Se}_3$ heterostructure enhances the total SOT by over 150%, primarily through modulation of the time-reversal-odd torque component.
method: The study employs first-principles calculations (DFT) to model the electronic structure and calculate the torkance tensor ($ oldsymbol{	au}$) as a function of ferroelectric polarization state.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a 2D van der Waals multiferroic heterostructure, specifically $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2/	ext{In}_2	ext{Se}_3$. The physics relies on the coupling between ferroelectric polarization switching and spin-orbit torque generation.
key_observables: Total torkance magnitude ($| oldsymbol{	au}|$), $z$-component of time-reversal-odd torque, magnetic moments of Fe atoms, electronic states near $\Gamma$ on the Fermi surface.
important_parameters: Ferroelectric polarization direction (up/down), magnetization orientation (in-plane vs. out-of-plane).
main_assumptions: The calculations utilize DFT with specific pseudopotentials and include a van der Waals correction; the analysis assumes SOT is governed by the time-reversal-odd component modulated by polarization.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates both standard current-induced SOT in FM/NM structures and, crucially, how ferroelectric polarization switching alters the torque magnitude in multiferroic heterostructures.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for tunable SOT in vdW systems; it then details the theoretical framework using DFT to calculate torkance based on polarization state; finally, it presents quantitative results showing the large enhancement of SOT upon ferroelectric switching and links this effect to electronic reconstruction.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter spintronics rather than fundamental quantum information protocols, the concept of electrically controlling magnetic properties via emergent coupling mechanisms (ferroelectricity $\leftrightarrow$ magnetism) is highly relevant to advanced quantum device architectures.
